scope_options.label: Cosmetic refresh
scope_options.description: New taps and shower fittings, a sanitaryware swap, paint and a mirror. No retiling and no waterproofing work. Quantity is the number of bathrooms.

scope_options.label: Retile and refit (keep waterproofing and pipes)
scope_options.description: New floor and wall tiles and new fittings, keeping the existing waterproofing and concealed supply and drain lines. Interior Decor Designs says this is only viable if the existing waterproofing is under 5 years old; ask for a leak and pressure check first. Quantity is the number of bathrooms.

scope_options.label: Full renovation
scope_options.description: Old tiles and fittings are removed down to the slab. The work then covers new waterproofing, concealed plumbing, floor and wall tiles, sanitaryware, taps and shower fittings, and electrical points. Moving the WC or shower to a new position costs extra. Quantity is the number of bathrooms.

materials.label: Ceramic tiles
materials.description: RealCostIQ pairs ceramic tiles with its budget package, and Asian Paints puts ceramic tile prices at about ₹60–₹200 per sq ft. Design Cafe advises anti-skid tiles for the floor.

duration_days.basis: Interior Decor Designs gives a typical timeline of 10–15 days, and Citi Design Studio, a Pune firm, gives 15–20 days for bathroom upgrades. NoBroker gives 2–4 weeks for small bathrooms and 3–5 weeks for a full renovation, and says rush jobs can finish in 10–14 days at 15–20% extra cost. Waterproofing needs curing time before tiling, and moving pipes or the WC adds days.

questions_to_ask: Is your price a lump sum per bathroom, a rate per sq ft, or itemised? If it is per sq ft, is that the floor area or the total tiled area of floor and walls?
Will you remove the old tiles down to the slab, or keep the existing waterproofing and pipes? If you keep them, how will you check them first?
Which waterproofing product will you use, how many coats, and how far up the walls will it go in the shower area?
Will you do a water (ponding) test after waterproofing and before tiling, and can I be present for it?
Are the concealed supply and drain pipes being replaced? Which pipe brand will you use, and will you pressure-test them before closing the walls?
Which brands and model numbers of tiles, sanitaryware, taps and shower fittings does the quote assume, and who buys them?
Does the price include demolition, debris removal from the building, electrical points, false ceiling and painting?
Is GST included in the price or extra?
What warranty do you give on waterproofing and on workmanship, and will you put it in writing?
How many working days will the job take, and will we have a usable bathroom during the work?
common_mistakes: Retiling without redoing the waterproofing underneath when the old waterproofing is not recent, so any existing leak into the flat below can continue.
Laying new tiles over old ones to save demolition cost, which raises the floor level and hides any failed waterproofing.
Not checking the floor slope towards the floor trap before tiling, which leaves water standing in corners.
Using glossy tiles on a wet bathroom floor instead of an anti-skid grade.
Comparing a per-bathroom lump sum with a per-sq-ft rate, or quotes that assume different tile and fitting brands, as if they covered the same scope.
Moving the WC or shower to a new position without budgeting for the extra plumbing work.
Closing the walls without pressure-testing new concealed supply lines.
Paying most of the amount upfront instead of linking payments to completed stages.
Starting demolition without informing the society office and the flat below.
quote_checklist: Price basis stated: per bathroom, per sq ft (and of which area), or itemised
Scope in writing: demolition, plumbing, waterproofing, tiling, sanitaryware, taps and shower fittings, electrical points, false ceiling, painting, debris removal
Bathroom floor size, and the wall tiling height
Tile type, size and brand, or a stated price allowance per sq ft
Waterproofing product, number of coats and where it is applied (floor, wall upturn, shower walls, around the floor trap and pipe openings)
Plumbing pipe brand and the number of inlet and outlet points, and whether any point is being moved
Sanitaryware and CP fitting brands and model numbers, or a stated allowance amount
Who supplies materials (contractor or owner) and who bears breakage and extra wastage
Timeline in working days, with a stage-wise payment schedule
Written warranty on waterproofing and workmanship
Whether GST is included or extra

faq.q: How much does a bathroom renovation cost in Pune?
faq.a: Our draft cost models, built from sources retrieved in October 2026, give these ranges per bathroom: budget ₹25,000–₹1,00,000 (expected about ₹50,000), standard ₹40,000–₹2,50,000 (about ₹1,65,000) and premium ₹1,10,000–₹5,00,000 (about ₹3,50,000). For a full renovation down to the slab in Pune, Interior Decor Designs gives ₹1.1–1.6 lakh (budget), ₹1.6–2.5 lakh (mid-range) and ₹3.4 lakh or more (premium) for a 5×7 to 6×8 ft bathroom. These are indicative ranges, not quotations.

faq.q: Why do bathroom renovation quotes vary so much?
faq.a: Quotes differ in scope (a cosmetic refresh, retiling, or a full renovation with new waterproofing and pipes), in tile and fitting brands, and in bathroom size. RealCostIQ estimates that CP fittings, shower cubicle, geyser and exhaust fan make up roughly 38–39% of the cost and sanitaryware roughly 20%, so the brands chosen change the total a lot. Ask each contractor to price the same scope and brands.

faq.q: How is a bathroom renovation priced?
faq.a: Most of the guides we used quote a lump sum per bathroom. Some Pune contractors listed on IndiaMART quote a rate per sq ft instead, and an itemised quote prices demolition, plumbing, waterproofing, tiling and fittings separately. If a quote is per sq ft, ask whether it means the floor area or the total tiled area of floor and walls, because the tiled wall area is usually larger than the floor.

faq.q: How long does a bathroom renovation take?
faq.a: Interior Decor Designs gives 10–15 days as typical, and Citi Design Studio in Pune gives 15–20 days. NoBroker gives 2–4 weeks for a small bathroom and 3–5 weeks for a full renovation, because waterproofing needs time to cure before tiling. Moving pipes or the WC adds time.

faq.q: Does a bathroom renovation need new waterproofing?
faq.a: If the floor tiles are being removed, the floor should be waterproofed again before new tiles go down. Interior Decor Designs says keeping the old waterproofing is only viable if it is under 5 years old. As a line item, NoBroker puts bathroom waterproofing at about ₹8,000–₹10,000 per bathroom plus 18% GST, and Livspace says it starts from ₹12,000 plus GST. Ask for a water test before tiling.

faq.q: Does moving the WC or shower add to the cost?
faq.a: Yes. Interior Decor Designs prices a full renovation with a layout change, such as moving the WC or shower point or adding a wet-dry partition, at ₹2.5–4.5 lakh. HomeLane says keeping the existing layout can save ₹20,000 to ₹80,000 by avoiding plumbing changes.

faq.q: How many bathrooms does the calculator assume for a flat?
faq.a: One for a 1 BHK, two for a 2 BHK (one attached, one common) and three for a 3 BHK, based on layouts Square Yards describes. Bathroom counts vary by project, especially in 3 BHK flats, so enter your own number if it differs.

faq.q: Do I need to inform my housing society?
faq.a: Check with your society office before work starts. Your society may have rules on working hours, noise, lift use and debris disposal. Inform the flat below as well, because demolition and waterproofing work affects the ceiling under your bathroom.
